facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule
fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area
teeth #15 and #16 were grossly carious
a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa
no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth
a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices
a provisional diagnosis of a periapical abscess was made
preoperative blood tests were within normal limits
curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue
a provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a slowly growing swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, along with the presence of grossly carious teeth and a mild periapical radiolucency, supports the diagnosis of a periapical granuloma, which is further confirmed by the histopathological examination of the gelatinous tissue obtained from curettage.

The patient's symptoms of a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa, along with the presence of a mild periapical radiolucency and the provisional diagnosis made, suggest the possibility of a periapical abscess, although the absence of tenderness on percussion and the nature of the tissue obtained from curettage make it less likely.

The patient's presentation of a slowly growing swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, along with the presence of grossly carious teeth and a mild periapical radiolucency, could also suggest the diagnosis of a periapical cyst, although the histopathological examination would be necessary to confirm this diagnosis.
